brief: A macOS menu bar app showing focus state through color and subtle motion — not a timer, an ambient presence

dominant_strengths: The blue orb has decent radial gradient craft and the soft glow gives a tactile, ambient focal point
Type hierarchy between 'Deep Focus' headline and the muted subtitle is clean and legible
dominant_weaknesses: Brief asks for a menu bar ambient presence; this is a giant modal-style card with three buttons — fundamentally wrong surface
Pause/Continue/Settings turn it back into a controllable timer-app, contradicting the 'not a timer' intent
Native macOS integration is shallow: generic gradient background, no menu bar popover chrome, vibrancy, or system materials
fix_priorities: Reframe as a true menu bar popover or a single tinted dot in the bar — kill the buttons and the card
Express state through color/motion alone (breathing hue, slow pulse) rather than a labeled headline + CTAs
Adopt native macOS materials: vibrancy blur, SF Pro, system corner radii, popover arrow
Replace the bottom 'sync' pill with a quieter status glyph integrated into the bar icon
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leans okay thanks to the orb, but behavioral overreaches with three buttons and reflective meaning is thin — it feels like a control panel, not a presence.
rationale.intent_fit: It largely misses the brief: an ambient menu-bar presence has been rendered as a centered modal with explicit controls, betraying the 'not a timer' premise.
